title: The Kindness Threshold

features.name: the line where gentleness stops
features.desc-on-touch: A fence, or maybe a shadow of one. Beyond it, the paddock continues but the quality of the light changes — less kind. The kindness learned it had an edge, and the edge learned it had been kind.

features.name: the well where kindness goes to drink
features.desc-on-touch: Water drawn up from deeper earth, cool and shared. People come here still, on both sides of the threshold. The well does not know it is an edge.

features.name: the homestead learning its own gentleness
features.desc-on-touch: A house that knows it stands on the kind side. Smoke rises from its chimney like a thank-you note. Windows show figures moving slowly, deliberately kind.

features.name: the gate that learned mercy
features.desc-on-touch: It still swings open, still lets people through. But it has learned to swing slowly, to creak a warning, to give things time to choose. The gate is kinder for knowing what lies beyond it.

features.name: the paddock that holds the light longer
features.desc-on-touch: Grass glowing gold in late afternoon. The kindness has made this place hold onto brightness a little longer than the fields beyond. You can feel it in the warmth.

features.name: the salt-lick where creatures learn to gather gently
features.desc-on-touch: Animals come here without fear. The kindness extends to them — they drink and graze without the tension that marks the other side. Gentleness is a frequency they can taste.

inscription: kindness has learned to have an edge without becoming cruel at the edge

file.note: Handwritten property register noting: 'The eastern line where the well-keeping tradition begins. Fence marks it. Water on both sides is the same water.'
